nodes.name: Theorem 4.1: $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{D^3}(M)$ homotopy finite
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be an irreducible 3-manifold with either empty or incompressible toroidal boundary, and let $D^3\subset \smash{\mathring{M}}$ be an embedded disk. 
    Then $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{D^3}(M)$ has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.20: Anosov $T^2$ bundle over $S^1$
nodes.statement: Let $M_A$ be a $T^2$-bundle over $S^1$ with Anosov monodromy $A\in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The inclusion $\mathrm{Isom}(M_A)\rightarrow \mathrm{Diff}(M_A)$ is a homotopy equivalence.  In particular, $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{D^3}(M_A)$ is homotopy finite.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.11
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact connected $3$-manifold and $T \subset \smash{\mathring{M}}$ a union of tori.
    Assume that $T$ is canonical, i.e.~the inclusion $\mathrm{Diff}(M, T) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is an equivalence.
    Suppose that any connected component $N$ of $M \smash{\mid} T$ satisfies:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        $(N \setminus \smash{\mathring{D}}^3, S^2)$ is hereditarily finite.
        \item
        For any non-empty union of boundary components $F \subset (2T \cap \partial N)$,
        $(N, F)$ is hereditarily finite. 
        \item The image of $\mathrm{Diff}(M, T) \to \pi_0(\mathrm{Diff}(T))$ is a finite group.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $(M \setminus \smash{\mathring{D}}^3, S^2)$ is hereditarily finite.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.19: Singular
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a Haken Seifert-fibered 3-manifold that is fiber-rigid, and let $D^3\subset M$ be an embedded disk. 
    Then $(M \setminus \smash{\mathring{D}}^3, S^2)$ is hereditarily finite and in particular $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{D^3}(M)$ is homotopy finite.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.17: Non-singular
nodes.statement:
Suppose $M$ admits a fiber-rigid Seifert fibering without singular fibers.
    Let $D^3\subset M$ be an embedded disk.
    Then $(M \setminus \smash{\mathring{D}}^3, S^2)$ is hereditarily finite and in particular
    $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{D^3}(M)$ is homotopy finite.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.2: $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M)$ homotopy finite
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact, connected, orientable $3$-manifold, and let $\emptyset \neq F \subseteq \partial M$ be a non-empty union of connected components.
    Assume that $\partial M \setminus F$ consists of spheres and incompressible tori.
    Then $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M)$ is homotopy finite.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.10, Lemma 2.11
nodes.statement:
The map
    \[
        \varphi_n\colon\mathrm{Sep}_n(M) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Sep}_0(M) = \mathrm{Sep}(M),
        \qquad
        (\Sigma_0 \subseteq \dots \subseteq \Sigma_n) \mapsto \Sigma_n
    \]
    is a finite covering.

Let $X$ be a $G$-locally retractile space 
    and assume that $X$ is locally path-connected.
    Then there is an equivalence
    \[
        X/\!\!/ G \simeq \coprod_{[x] \in X/G} B\mathrm{Stab}_G(x)
    \]
    where the coproduct runs over orbit representatives $[x]\in X/G$.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.8: $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M, \Sigma)$ homotopy finite
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact connected $3$-manifold, $\emptyset \neq F \subseteq \partial M$ a non-empty union of boundary components such that $\partial M \setminus F$ contains only spheres and incompressible tori, and let $\Sigma \in \mathrm{Sep}(M)$ be a separating system.
    Then $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M , \Sigma)$
    is homotopy finite.
nodes.section: Figure 5: Flowchart of the proof of 6.2. Note that the bottom central leaf is the root ver

nodes.name: Corollary 5.9
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a compact connected $3$-manifold, $F \subset \partial M$ a non-empty union of boundary components and $\Sigma \subset M$ a sphere system. 
    Suppose that 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[$(\ddagger)$]
        for every component $N \subseteq M \smash{\mid} \Sigma$ and every union of boundary components $F' \subseteq \partial N$ satisfying $F' \neq \emptyset$ and $F' \supseteq \partial N \cap F$ we know that  $ B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{F'}(N) $ is homotopy finite.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M, \Sigma)$ is homotopy finite.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.6: $\mathrm{Sep}^{\nparallel}(M)/\mathrm{Diff}_F(M)$ finite
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a 3-manifold with possibly empty boundary and $F \subseteq \partial M$ a union of boundary components. 
    Then the set $\mathrm{Sep}^{\nparallel}(M)/\mathrm{Diff}_F(M)$ is finite.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.4: $\widehat{M}$ irreducible
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $M$ is such that the manifold $\smash{\widehat{M}}$ obtained by filling all spherical boundary components is irreducible. Let $F \subseteq \partial M$ be a non-empty union of boundary components such that $\partial M \setminus F$ contains only spheres and incompressible tori.
    Then $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M)$ is homotopy finite.
nodes.section: Figure 5: Flowchart of the proof of 6.2. Note that the bottom central leaf is the root ver

nodes.name: Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $M$ is a connected 3-manifold and $F \subseteq \partial M$ is a union of connected components of its boundary.
    Let $B \subset \smash{\mathring{M}}$ be a finite union of disjoint disks.
    Then we have equivalences 
    \[
        B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{F \sqcup B}(M) \simeq
        B\!\mathrm{Diff}_{F \sqcup \partial B}( M\setminus \smash{\mathring{B}} ) 
        \quad \text{ and } \quad 
        B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M, B)
        \simeq B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M \setminus \smash{\mathring{B}}, \partial B) .
    \]
    Suppose moreover that $B\!\mathrm{Diff}_F(M)$ is homotopy finite, then so are the above spaces.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.4: $M$ irreducible
nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be an irreducible $3$-manifold that is either hyperbolic or Seifert-fibered.
    Let $F \subset \partial M$ be a non-empty union of boundary components, including all the compressible ones. 
    Then $(M, F)$ is hereditarily finite.
